records.source_first_note: Complete Hindi field read. Jarir reports his pledge to the Prophet: testimony, prayer, zakat, hearing/obeying and goodwill. Keep the parenthetic appointed-leader object because the following obedience pronoun depends on it; it is substantive scope, not an optional synonym.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve all pledge clauses and the own-appointed-leader object of hearing, which supplies the antecedent for subsequent obedience. Jarir is narrating his pledge, not supplying an anonymous compiler ruling.

Complete Hindi field read. The Ibn Umar chain supplies an actual Prophetic prohibition concerning a townsman selling a countryman’s goods. The final same-was-said-by-Ibn-Abbas sentence is a transmission comparison rather than an independently quoted new body; keeping that tail in context is justified.

Complete Urdu field read. Keep the full Ibn Umar-attributed prohibition. The closing یہی ابن عباس comparison is source transmission context, with its words preserved and no reconstructed separate quotation.

Complete Hindi field read. Anas says we were forbidden to have a townsman sell a countryman’s trade goods. The prohibitor is not explicitly named in this field, so classify the actual Companion testimony without supplying a Prophetic speaker from nearby entries.

Complete Urdu field read. The passive ہمیں اس سے روکا گیا supplies a finite Anas report but does not itself name who prohibited the act. Retain the complete statement under Anas’s actual voice and leave that authority qualified.

Complete Hindi field read. Both prohibitions are explicitly attributed. Retain the parenthetic trading-caravans object of going ahead to meet; removing it would broaden the first prohibition to unspecified meetings. Preserve the townsman/countryman condition separately.

Complete Urdu field read. The trading-caravans phrase specifies the object of the first prohibition and is substantive scope. Both actual prohibitions are supplied, with no extra timing or purchase verb to add.

Complete Hindi field read. Tawus asks Ibn Abbas the meaning of an explicitly quoted Prophetic instruction, and Ibn Abbas supplies the broker answer. Preserve the actual named dialogue and the embedded quote, keeping the explanatory answer in the Companion’s voice.

Complete Urdu field read. The complete Tawus/Ibn-Abbas question-and-answer is a finite attributed explanation containing the quoted Prophetic phrase. It is not an anonymous compiler gloss, and the answer must not be relabelled as direct Prophetic speech.

Complete Hindi field read. The milk-accumulated goat return/one-sa instruction is introduced as Ibn Masud’s statement; the later caravan prohibition is expressly Prophetic. Separate those voices. Retain the parenthetic return-the-goat predicate, which completes the actual first instruction.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve Ibn Masud’s goat/one-sa statement and the separately explicit Prophetic caravan prohibition. The parenthetic وہ بکری پھیر دے is an actual imperative predicate, not disposable lexical apparatus.

Complete Hindi field read. The identical Musaddad/Yahya/Ubaydullah/Nafi/Abdullah chain is repeated and stops at the said-that link both times. No actual numbered report body is printed; retain all Hindi text as reviewed source context.
Complete Urdu field read. Two copies of the same chain end with بیان کیا کہ and provide no matn. Entire field is reviewed context; do not fill it from Arabic or English.

Complete Arabic field read. It supplies the Abdullah chain and an actual market-food account: buying at the upper market, selling in place and the Prophet forbidding sale until transfer. Preserve the finite body and the exact transfer wording without inventing a destination.

Complete English field read. It supplies buying food at the market head, reselling on the spot and the Prophet’s restriction until bringing it to places. The parenthetic their is a lexical possessor gloss that can remain context; do not substitute the Arabic wording or extend the printed destination.

Complete Roman Urdu field read. The source repeats the full chain twice and stops at bayan kiya ke; no body follows. Retain it completely as reviewed context without importing either available narrative sibling.

Complete Urdu field read. Abu al-Minhal’s question and the two Companions’ reciprocal deference are actual dialogue framing, followed by their transmitted Prophetic credit prohibition. The gold/silver-exchange definition of bay-sarf is lexical context. Do not reconcile the name with Hindi.

Complete Hindi field read independently at its own provider ID. It prints the same question, reciprocal deference and transmitted prohibition, but remains a separate source occurrence. The bay-sarf definition is context; keep the Companion dialogue/appraisal and Prophetic words accurately attributed.

Complete Hindi field read. The Abu Bakra report preserves like-metal equality as an exception and the two cross-metal permissions. Keep all qualifications; do not insert an unprinted spot-payment condition or reinterpret the list from another report.
